ch06.card: Part 5 of 8. Deciding when it is done.
ch06.s01.c1: The model thinks in rounds, one lap at a time.
ch06.s01.c2: The stop switch decides when the thinking is finished.
ch06.s01.c3: It is built, but it has never been run.
ch06.s02.c1: The older design had a dial: the same number of rounds for every question, set by hand (12 in the tested model, 8 in another).
ch06.s02.c2: Easy questions may need fewer rounds. Hard questions may need more.
ch06.s03.c1: We turned the dial down on one trained copy, with no new practice.
ch06.s03.c2: Points out of 100, on 6,040 questions kept aside (called pooled-5).
ch06.s03.c3: Trained at 12 rounds it scored 73.01. With 2 rounds, 29.30. With 1 round, 20.00. With 0 rounds, 0.66.
ch06.s04.c1: Chain-5 is a set of 1,000 multi-step questions, scored on the same trained copy.
ch06.s04.c2: On pooled-5, 1 round scored 20.00. On chain-5 it scored 0.0, and 1.1 at 2 rounds.
ch06.s04.c3: At the full 12 rounds chain-5 scored 99.9. So this copy needed more rounds on multi-step questions than on pooled-5.
ch06.s05.c1: Older models were trained for 8 rounds. In a round-count test on two copies, the score on practice-like questions stopped rising at 8 rounds.
ch06.s05.c2: On all 8 copies we checked (those two and six more), running 16 rounds scored 0.8 to 1.9 points lower than 8 rounds.
ch06.s05.c3: So too few rounds hurt, and too many may hurt too.
ch06.s06.c1: After every round, the stop switch, a small head, reads one of the thinker's note cards.
ch06.s06.c2: It gives a number from 0 to 1. At 0.5 or more, the thinking stops.
ch06.s06.c3: It always runs at least 1 round, and never more than 32.
ch06.s06.c4: The stop switch has 257 numbers when each card has 256, and 513 when each has 512.
ch06.s07.c1: There is one stop for the whole answer, not one stop per call.
ch06.s07.c2: Built, not tested: a call to the calculator may follow any round from round 2 up to 32.
ch06.s07.c3: In the built training code, about a quarter of the questions add 0 to 2 extra thinking rounds before a call.
ch06.s08.c1: Training gives every round a label: stop, or keep going.
ch06.s08.c2: The label says stop when the answer is right now, or when no later round is right.
ch06.s08.c3: So the stop switch is also taught to stop on questions it cannot solve.
ch06.s09.c1: Practice uses batches of questions, and some batches run only 8 rounds. There, a question first right at round 10 looks never right.
ch06.s09.c2: So the label says stop at round 1, and the stop switch would learn to stop too early.
ch06.s09.c3: Fix: the stop switch learns only from batches that run all 32 rounds, about 1 in 4.
ch06.s10.c1: The label only sees the rounds a question actually ran.
ch06.s10.c2: So a stop that fires early may never be shown a later right answer (suggested).
ch06.s10.c3: The first run is planned to report how often questions stop early, and their answers. This is reported only, not a pass mark.
ch06.s11.c1: Key pass marks (bars the test must reach) were written before any run. They are targets, not results.
ch06.s11.c2: On average, 1-step questions must use at most half the rounds of the longest ones (code: 11 steps; plan: 12).
ch06.s11.c3: Always-32 is the same model forced to think all 32 rounds. Practised questions: within 1 point. Longer chains: within 2.
ch06.s11.c4: It fails if it never stops early (rounds within 10% of 32), or if longer chains fall over 5 below always-32.
ch06.s12.c1: No build switch removes the stop. The switches cover things like Gemma and calls, not the stop.
ch06.s12.c2: A trained copy can still be run with the stop ignored and a forced number of rounds, as a test.
ch06.s12.c3: The nearest model with no stop is the outside-calculator model (T1SDR), with a fixed 8 rounds.
ch06.s12.c4: The stop has never run. Its first run is planned after the separate G1 size test finishes (not covered here).
ch06.s13.c1: People talk about fast thinking and slow thinking. Few rounds is like the fast kind, many rounds like the slow kind.
ch06.s13.c2: We suggest one looped thinker gives both, so no separate fast and slow model is needed (suggested, not tested).
ch06.s13.c3: To remember: the stop switch decides, the limit is 32 rounds, and the stop is built but not yet run.
